overview: This bill, the ADS for Mental Health Services Act, requires the largest social media platforms, those that earn money from ads and have more than 100 million monthly users, to report each year to the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) on the free public service ads they run about mental health. The reports would cover how many such ads the platform ran and what share of all its ads they made up, their estimated dollar value, and how many pointed to local or free mental and behavioral health resources, such as help with suicide prevention, eating disorders, substance abuse, or social isolation. The FTC would then send Congress a public summary each year. The bill does not require platforms to run any ads, and it expires after five years. The Senate passed it on December 9, 2025, and as of December 10, 2025, it was awaiting action in the House.
for: Supporters say public reporting will show whether big platforms are doing their part to connect users, especially young people, with mental health help, and could encourage them to do more.
against: Critics say the bill adds a paperwork requirement that does not itself get anyone help, and that counting free ads says little about whether they actually reach or benefit people in need.
